text: dsh-voice（DSH 网页插件）：为 DeepSeek Harness 网页界面加入语音朗读和语音输入。它在助手回复旁注册朗读按钮，在输入框旁注册麦克风，并提供 Voice 设置和可选侧栏阅读器。用户可朗读回复、自动朗读新回复、录制语音并将转写文字插入输入框，也可配置 TTS/STT 提供商与语言选项。适合希望免手动阅读或语音输入 DSH 对话的网页用户。语音处理使用所选引擎；是否需要凭据取决于配置的提供商。

dsh-voice adds speech playback and dictation to DSH web. It puts read-aloud controls by replies and a microphone by the composer, with Voice settings and an optional sidebar reader. Users can listen, dictate into the composer, and select providers and languages. Credentials vary by provider.
想让 DSH 网页版把助手回复读出来。
我想直接对着麦克风说话，把转写内容放进对话输入框。
Can DSH read new chat replies aloud and let me dictate prompts in the web composer?
dsh-voice 的功能「网页语音朗读与听写」：在助手回复旁提供朗读控制，并在输入框旁提供麦克风；录音经 STT 转写后，可插入当前输入草稿。可通过 Voice 设置选择引擎和自动朗读选项。
dsh-voice 使用前须知：使用 TTS 时，输入的回复文本会交给所选语音引擎处理；听写时，录制的音频会交给所选 STT 引擎处理。具体接收方取决于用户配置。
dsh-voice 使用前须知：远程语音提供商可能需要各自的凭据；插件支持从环境变量、文件或 DSH 凭据存储解析凭据，实际要求取决于所选提供商。

text:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · restart dsh web, then pick your speech providers in Settings, Voice：- A speaker on every finished assistant reply (and a `{ }` button that reads the code blocks).
- A microphone in the composer, with an optional polish pass that fixes punctuation without translating.
- **Several speech providers at once**, configured in Settings > Voice, each with a Test button.
- **Per-language routing**: English, Italian, Greek (and any language you add) each get their own provider, model, voice and speed.
- **In-text language markers** to switch language mid-text.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · restart dsh web, then pick your speech providers in Settings, Voice：- **Language detection** per sentence, with a DSH model for the unsure ones, and a language badge while reading.
- **Highlighting** of the sentence and the word being read, and opt-in **auto-read** of new replies.

- A **TTS Reader** sidebar tab, push-to-talk **dictation** at the composer cursor, and **keyboard shortcuts**.

Status: 2.0.0. 23 provider types, EU vendors first; see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Runs on DSH 0.2.x (tested on 0.2.1) and DSH 0.1.5.

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` lists it in the profile bundles; restart `dsh web` to load the host half. `lib/` is committed, so no build step is needed. From a checkout instead: `git clone https://github.com/lucagiftzek/dsh-voice`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD/dsh-voice`. Then open Settings > Voice, add a provider and press Test.

text: @lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Providers：Settings > Voice lists providers in three groups, **EU first**, then **Others**, then **Self-hosted**, each with a residency badge (EU, EU region available, outside the EU, self-hosted, on device) and a timing badge (word timings, or estimated). "Add provider" lists every type with a one-line description and a docs link. Several instances of one type are normal (a local server plus a relayed one, two Azure regions). Keys never reach the browser, and a Test button on every row speaks a short phrase and transcribes it back (a speech-to-text-only provider borrows the spoken sample from another provider).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Providers："Word timings" means the provider returns when each word is spoken, so the word highlight is exact; otherwise the highlight is estimated from the audio length (sentence highlight always works). A provider without a language in its list never receives that language through automatic routing. Status marks: *(planned)* has no public API documentation yet, *(unverified)* or *(partly verified)* means some request shapes could not be confirmed against vendor documentation on the date given under "Verification" in `docs/PROVIDERS.md`.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Credentials：An instance stores a pointer, resolved at call time:

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `env:NAME` | an environment variable of the DSH web process |
| `file:/path#NAME` | a `NAME=value` line of a dotenv-style file |
| `file:/path` | the whole file |
| `dsh-ref:NAME` | `refs.NAME` in the DSH credential store |
| `a\|b` | the first pointer that resolves |
| a literal key typed in Settings | stored in the plugin's own `vault.json` (mode 0600), never in a settings file; shown as `__set__` |

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Credentials：With no settings at all, the instances are discovered from the same environment variables 1.x read (`MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `MIMO_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` / `MIMO_TOKEN_PLAN_BASE_URL` or the MiMo credentials file, `TTS_API_KEY` with `DSH_VOICE_TTS_HOST/PORT`, `GREY_TTS_URL` / `GREY_TTS_API_KEY`, `DSH_VOICE_LFM3_HOST/PORT`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `ALIBABA_*`), so an existing install keeps working without a config edit.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Routing：`perLanguage.<lang>.tts` and `.stt` hold `{provider, model, voice, speed, fallback[]}`. The shipped value for every language is `provider: auto`, which is the built-in 1.x chain: English goes to MiMo, then Mistral; Greek, Italian and the rest go to the local TTS server (for example Maya1 and Whisper); ElevenLabs stays selectable but out of automatic routing. "Apply recommended" in Settings fills in the EU-first recommendation per language (Mistral for English and Italian, ElevenLabs for Greek, with fallbacks) for you to review and save.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Per-language defaults：The shipped value of every language is `auto` (the 1.x chain above), so an existing install behaves exactly as before. "Apply recommended" fills a row with the EU-first suggestion below; review it and Save. Nothing is applied for you.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Per-language defaults：| Language | Read aloud, recommended | Fallbacks | Dictation, recommended |
|---|---|---|---|
| English | Mistral `voxtral-mini-tts-3-0`, voice `gb_oliver_neutral` | MiMo, ElevenLabs, browser | Mistral transcribe, then MiMo, then a local server |
| Italian | Mistral `voxtral-mini-tts-3-0`, voice `voice_482` | ElevenLabs, LFM3, local server, browser | local faster-whisper, then Mistral |
| Greek | ElevenLabs `eleven_multilingual_v2` (exact word timings in Greek; Azure with `el-GR-AthinaNeural` is the other cloud choice) | LFM3, local server, browser | local faster-whisper, then ElevenLabs Scribe |
| any other | first enabled provider whose language list covers it | browser | first multilingual provider |

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Per-language defaults：Greek has no preset voice at Mistral, Amazon Polly, Deepgram Aura or Kokoro (and AssemblyAI's best model and XTTS lack it), so check the language list a provider declares (shown under its row and in the table above) before choosing it.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Per-language defaults：Resolution for one segment: marker override, then the manual pick in the composer, then the language row, then the `*` row, then any enabled instance that covers the language, then the browser voice. Routing chooses by availability; a failure inside a segment never switches provider mid-sentence.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Language markers：| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[[el]]` | Greek from here on (sticky) |
| `[[it]]...[[/]]` | Italian for the span, then back |
| `[[auto]]` | back to automatic detection |
| `[[el voice=x provider=y model=z speed=1.1]]`, `[[pause 600]]` | per-span options, a pause in ms |
| `<!--lang:el-->`, `<!--lang:/-->` | the same, invisible in rendered markdown |
| `\[[el]]` | literal text |
@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Language markers：Markers inside code are ignored, anything else in double brackets (a wiki link) stays text, and every marker is removed before the text is spoken.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Language detection：Explicit beats detected: a marked span is never re-detected. Unmarked text is split into sentences (the Greek question mark `;` ends a sentence, the ano teleia does not), then:
@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Language detection：The speaker shows the language being read as a small badge (EN, IT, EL), with how it was decided in the tooltip.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · TTS Reader tab：A tab of dsh-better-sidebar (id `dsh-tts-reader:main`, title "TTS Reader", so a saved sidebar layout keeps it; it replaces the separate dsh-tts-reader package, which is now a stub that registers nothing). Text comes from typing or pasting, the current reply, the selection in the chat, or a `.txt`, `.md` or `.html` file opened from this computer (read in the browser, nothing is uploaded). Buttons insert `[[en]]`, `[[it]]`, `[[el]]` and `[[/]]` at the cursor (around the selection when there is one); with Voxtral TTS 3 a menu inserts its emotion, pace and sound tags, which no other engine receives. The provider, model, voice and speed apply to this read only. The reading view shows the text per language with a chip each and the same highlight as the chat. **Download audio** writes the whole text as one MP3, or as one WAV when the voices differ in format or the text has pauses (the browser voice cannot be exported). The sidebar is optional: without dsh-better-sidebar everything else loads.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Dictation：Click the microphone to start and stop, or hold it and release to send (`dictation.mode: push-to-talk` makes holding the only way). While recording a level meter and a cancel button appear. The chip next to the mic picks the language (Auto, or one of the enabled languages, whose row of the language table chooses the transcription provider); in Auto it shows what was heard. The transcript is polished by the DSH model chosen in Settings (punctuation and casing only, never a translation; Mistral and a local model stay as fallbacks) and inserted at the composer cursor (`dictation.insert`: `caret`, `append`, `replace`).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Keyboard shortcuts：| Action | Default |
|---|---|
| Read the last reply | `Alt+Shift+R` |
| Play / pause | `Alt+Shift+P` |
| Stop | `Alt+Shift+S` |
| Next / previous sentence | `Alt+Shift+.` / `Alt+Shift+,` |
| Faster / slower | `Alt+Shift+=` / `Alt+Shift+-` |
| Dictation (tap toggles, hold to talk) | `Alt+Shift+M` |
| Cycle the dictation language | `Alt+Shift+L` |

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Keyboard shortcuts：Change or clear them in Settings > Voice (`shortcuts.*`). Keys are matched by their physical position, so a Greek or Italian layout keeps them. The DSH composer uses Alt or Shift with the arrow keys, Enter combinations and Ctrl+O, and DSH owns bare Escape; the defaults avoid all of them. Every control is a labelled button, toggles report their state, and status lines are announced politely to screen readers.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Settings：Settings > Voice edits everything through `GET/PATCH /api/voice/settings` (the read redacts secrets; the write needs a short-lived capability token, the harness session cookie and a same-origin request). Where the values live depends on the DSH line (`lib/dual-settings.js`, shared with the other plugins of the 0.2 migration): on 0.1.5 the namespace `dsh-voice` of DSH Settings; on 0.2.x this plugin's row in the profile configuration, through the exported `Config` whose top-level keys are all live, with a one-time import of an old `dsh-voice:` section; without a settings service, the plugin settings file (`$DSH_VOICE_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.config/dsh-voice/settings.json`). Keys typed in Settings never land in any of these: they go to `vault.json` (mode 0600) next to it. Behind a reverse proxy, add the public host name to `security.trustedHosts` (on 0.1.5: `dsh-voice: { security: { trustedHosts: [your.host] } }` in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Settings：A Settings write is also checked for where it sends a key: a cloud provider's base URL (and its WebSocket or TTS host option) must be `https` on a public host, so a stored credential cannot be pointed at an internal service or a host of the writer's choosing; self-hosted types (ElevenLabs-compatible, Kokoro, LFM3, Piper, XTTS, OpenAI-compatible) may use loopback and LAN addresses; a value that equals the current environment-configured one (a relay) is always accepted; and a stored key (`vault:<id>`) can only be used by its own provider.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · HTTP routes：Unchanged from 1.x: `GET /api/voice/config`, `GET /api/voice/quota`, `POST /api/voice/tts`, `POST /api/voice/stt`, `POST /api/voice/polish`. New: `GET /api/voice/session`, `GET|PATCH /api/voice/settings`, `POST /api/voice/test`, `GET /api/voice/voices`, `GET /api/voice/models`, `GET /api/voice/doctor` (read-only self-check, same gate as the settings read; probes only loopback and self-hosted engines with a 2 s GET), `POST /api/voice/detect` (segments with language, source and confidence; the model pass included), and `POST /api/voice/tts?alignment=1` (JSON with base64 audio and word timings where the provider has them).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · HTTP routes：The 1.x routes stay open to same-origin callers (other plugins such as a notes plugin call `/stt` and `/polish`) but refuse a browser request from another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` or a foreign `Origin`), so a third-party page cannot spend credits. Rate limits per minute (`security.rateLimit`): `ttsPerMin` 60, `sttPerMin` 30, `detectPerMin` 60, `polishPerMin` 30.

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · When something goes wrong：- Ask your agent to load the **`voice-doctor`** skill (bundled; see
  [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#start-here) if it is not listed). If it is not
  registered yet, copy it by hand:
  `P=$(node -p "require('path').dirname(require.resolve('dsh-voice/package.json',{paths:[(process.env.DSH_HOME||require('os').homedir()+'/.dsh')+'/profiles/web']}))")`
  then `mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" && cp -r "$P/skills/voice-doctor" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"`.
- Run the self-check: `GET /api/voice/doctor` (read-only, no secrets in the output).
- Every error carries a stable `code`: [docs/ERRORS.md](docs/ERRORS.md).

@lucagiftzek/dsh-voice README · Development：```
npm install          # esbuild and react for the build and the render test
npm run build        # src/client -> lib/client.js, verified before it is written
npm test             # node --test
npm run check        # bundle and provider docs up to date + tests

`lib/client.js` is generated: edit `src/client/` and rebuild. The host half uses Node built-ins only.

Kill switch: add `- id: voice` with `disabled: true` to the web profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and restart dsh-web.
